column3: NASB renders “be overcome” as “is caught” and “considering yourself” as “each one looking to yourself.”
NASB reads the imperative “fulfill,” as other manuscripts do; the critical text has the future “you will fulfill.”
NASB renders “test” as “examine” and “ground of boasting” as “reason for boasting.”
NASB renders “grow weary” as “lose heart” and “not giving up” as “if we do not grow weary.”
NASB renders “I have written” as “I am writing.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Christ”); “have a fair appearance” is rendered “make a good showing,” and it adds “try to.”
NASB renders “never would it be” as “may it never be” and reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text without “in Christ Jesus.”
NASB renders “who will walk by this rule” as “those who will walk by this rule” and moves “mercy” forward.
NASB follows the critical text without “Lord”; “marks” is rendered “brand-marks,” and “give troubles” is “cause trouble.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus subscription.
